records.title: `docs_present()` ignores cite-only docs-backed trees
records.divergence_description: The startup warning path still treats cite-only documentation trees as docless even though the canonical documentation-state helpers classify the same trees as docs-backed.
records.documented_intent: REQ-001 requires plaintext files under `reference_docs/cite/` to count as valid documentation input on every startup path that decides whether the run is docs-backed or code-only.
records.code_behavior: `bin/run_playbook.py:1568-1574` only scans top-level files, while `_evaluate_documentation_state()` and `formal_docs_guard_banner()` recurse into `reference_docs/cite/` and accept cite-only trees (`bin/run_playbook.py:1617-1621`, `1666-1669`).
records.disposition_rationale: The divergence is entirely in the executable predicate used by the startup warning paths; the documented contract and the other code surfaces already agree on the intended cite-only behavior.
records.proposed_fix: Make `docs_present()` use the same recognized-plaintext predicate as `_evaluate_documentation_state()` and `formal_docs_guard_banner()`. See `quality/patches/BUG-001-fix.patch`.

records.title: `docs_present()` uses a broader predicate than the rest of the documentation-state logic
records.divergence_description: The warning helper counts README-only and binary-only trees as docs-present while also missing cite-only trees, so operator-visible startup messaging disagrees with the runner's stored documentation state.
records.documented_intent: REQ-002 requires warnings, state evaluation, and the formal-doc banner to share one recognized-plaintext rule across README-only, binary-only, cite-only, and top-level plaintext trees.
records.code_behavior: `bin/run_playbook.py:1568-1574` treats any non-dot top-level file as documentation, whereas `_reference_docs_plaintext()` filters to `.md`/`.txt`, skips `README.md`, and recurses into `cite/` (`bin/run_playbook.py:1583-1595`).
records.disposition_rationale: All three failing cells come from the same helper drift inside the startup warning path; no documentation or schema change is needed.
records.proposed_fix: Route `docs_present()` through `_reference_docs_plaintext()` or an equivalent shared helper so every documentation-state surface uses the same predicate. See `quality/patches/BUG-002-fix.patch`.
records.consolidation_rationale: A single predicate mismatch in `docs_present()` causes the README-only, binary-only, and cite-only parity failures.

records.title: Tier 4 ingest leaks nested non-`cite/` archives into Phase 1 context
records.divergence_description: The ingest pipeline treats every non-`cite/` plaintext file in the `reference_docs/` subtree as Tier 4 context, not just the documented top-level files.
records.documented_intent: REQ-003 requires Tier 4 ingest to stay limited to the documented top-level `reference_docs/` plaintext surface unless the contract is explicitly widened.
records.code_behavior: `bin/reference_docs_ingest.py:90-93` recursively enumerates the full tree, `_collect()` assigns `tier=4` to every non-`cite/` plaintext file (`189-227`), and `load_tier4_context()` returns those records directly (`263-276`).
records.disposition_rationale: The contract and the Phase 2 requirement are explicit about top-level-only Tier 4 scope; the bug is the missing filter in the ingest implementation.
records.proposed_fix: Restrict Tier 4 collection to top-level `reference_docs/*.{md,txt}` files while preserving `cite/` recursion for formal-doc ingest. See `quality/patches/BUG-003-fix.patch`.

records.title: Bootstrap mirroring drops the `cite/` formal-doc bucket
records.divergence_description: The bootstrap mirror helper preserves top-level plaintext docs but never copies the source-side `cite/` subtree into `reference_docs/cite/`.
records.documented_intent: REQ-004 requires bootstrap mirroring to preserve the top-level-vs-`cite/` placement semantics of the source bootstrap corpus.
records.code_behavior: `bin/bootstrap_self_audit_docs.py:50-61` creates `reference_docs/cite/` and then iterates only `SOURCE_DIR.iterdir()`, skipping subdirectories entirely.
records.disposition_rationale: The missing behavior is confined to the mirroring helper; the destination layout and the ingest contract already define the correct placement.
records.proposed_fix: Mirror both eligible top-level docs and eligible files under `docs_gathered/cite/` into the corresponding destination buckets. See `quality/patches/BUG-004-fix.patch`.

records.title: The Phase 1 validator accepts long placeholders instead of the written gate contract
records.divergence_description: The mechanical Phase 1 validator enforces only file existence, a 120-line minimum, and a generic findings regex even though the skill names a much stronger gate with exact headings and analytical minima.
records.documented_intent: REQ-005 requires the mechanical validator to reject `quality/EXPLORATION.md` artifacts that omit the exact mandatory sections and content depth named by the Phase 2 gate.
records.code_behavior: `bin/run_state_lib.py:171-198` stops after the line-count and generic findings checks, while `SKILL.md:1260-1273` defines the full required heading and content set.
records.disposition_rationale: The skill prose already defines the authoritative contract; the runtime validator is simply too weak and needs to enforce the documented checks.
records.proposed_fix: Extend `validate_phase_artifacts(..., 1)` to check the exact required headings and the Phase 2 gate's analytical minima before it returns success. See `quality/patches/BUG-005-fix.patch`.
records.consolidation_rationale: All absent cells are omitted by the same Phase 1 validation branch, so a single validator expansion closes the full missing gate contract.

records.title: Archive bug counting ignores canonical titled headings
records.divergence_description: Archive summaries split `BUGS.md` only on bare `### BUG-NNN` headings, so the canonical titled form `### BUG-NNN: Title` is silently skipped.
records.documented_intent: REQ-006 requires archive rendering to preserve bug counts from the canonical titled heading form used everywhere else in the playbook.
records.code_behavior: `bin/archive_lib.py:69` defines `_BUG_HEADING_PATTERN` without an optional title suffix, and `_extract_bug_counts()` depends on that pattern to segment the file (`321-338`).
records.disposition_rationale: The archive parser is the only outlier; the canonical heading form is already established by the rest of the protocol.
records.proposed_fix: Allow `_BUG_HEADING_PATTERN` to match an optional `: Title` suffix so canonical `BUGS.md` sections are counted. See `quality/patches/BUG-006-fix.patch`.
